00022 /**
00023  * @brief _HxImageDescription_t is a structure containing fields that describe
00024  * the dimensions and format of an image.  HxImageDescriptionGetBounds,
00025  * HxImageDescriptionGetFormat, and HxImageDescriptionGetData can be used to
00026  * retrieve image information once the structure has been created.
00027  *
00028  * The structure can be created in two ways.
00029  *
00030  * If the source data is uncompressed raster data, the application uses 
00031  * HxImageDescriptionNewFromData, providing image parameters together with a
00032  * pointer to the source data.  The image structure is returned.
00033  *
00034  * If the source data is a coming from a compressed image file, the
00035  * application uses HxImageDescriptionNewFromFile, sending the filename
00036  * string, including the path.  The image structure is returned.
00037  *
00038  * This is an opaque structure.
00039  */
00040 typedef struct _HxImageDescription_t    HxImageDescription_t;

00370 /**
00371  * @brief               Draw an image description
00372  *
00373  * HxImageDescriptionDraw draws an image based on the pointer to a
00374  * HxImageDescription_t structure obtained from a prior call to 
00375  * HxImageDescriptionNewFromFile or HxImageDescriptionNewFromData.  
00376  *
00377  * pDstImage can be either an on-screen window, or an off-screen
00378  * canvas.  If NULL, the application window is used.
00379  *
00380  * The bounds of the source data is defined by pSrcRect.  If pSrcRect
00381  * is NULL, the entire source image is used.
00382  *
00383  * The bounds into which the source data is stretched is defined by
00384  * pDstRect.  If pDstRect is NULL, the bounds of the main application
00385  * window is used.
00386  *
00387  * The source data is stretch-blitted to the destination, based on the
00388  * source and destination rectangles.
00389  *
00390  * If the source data has an alpha channel or if it was loaded from a
00391  * file format that supports a transparent color index (or source
00392  * color key), then this function sets the blitting flags for the
00393  * destination image appropriately.  If the application wants to set
00394  * custom blit flags, then use HxImageDescriptionDrawWithFlags.
00395  *
00396  * @param pDescription  IN:     Pointer to HxImageDescription_t
00397  * @param pDstImage     IN:     Destination image, widget, window,
00398  *                              or NULL to use application window.
00399  * @param pSrcRect      IN:     Bounds of source data to be drawn, or NULL
00400  * @param pDstRect      IN:     Destination bounds where source drawn, or NULL
00401  *
00402  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00403  *                              Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if allocation fails.
00404  *
00405  **/
00406 HxResult HxImageDescriptionDraw(HxImageDescription_t* pDescription,
00407                                 HxImage_t* pDstImage,
00408                                 const HxRectangle_t* pSrcRect,
00409                                 const HxRectangle_t* pDstRect);
00410 
00411 /**
00412  * @brief               Draw an image description with blit flags
00413  *
00414  * HxImageDescriptionDrawWithFlags is a variation of HxImageDescriptionDraw,
00415  * and allows the application to customize the blit flags.
00416  *
00417  * This function will call HxGraphicsSetBlitFlags on the destination
00418  * image using the value passed in as the flags parameter.  Use
00419  * kHxBlitBlendAlphaChannel to do alpha blending or use
00420  * kHxBlitSrcColorKey to mask out a color from the image.  If you are
00421  * copying an image and want to preserve the alpha channel, use
00422  * kHxBlitNoFX.
00423  *
00424  * See hxuitypes.h for a full listing of HxBlitFlags and their
00425  * descriptions.
00426  *
00427  * @param pDescription  IN:     Pointer to HxImageDescription_t
00428  * @param pDstImage     IN:     Destination image, widget, window,
00429  *                              or NULL to use application window.
00430  * @param pSrcRect      IN:     Bounds of source data to be drawn, or NULL
00431  * @param pDstRect      IN:     Destination bounds where source drawn, or NULL
00432  * @param flags         IN:     Blitting flags (see hxuitypes.h)
00433  *
00434  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00435  *                              Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if allocation fails.
00436  *
00437  **/
00438 HxResult HxImageDescriptionDrawWithFlags(HxImageDescription_t* pDescription,
00439                                          HxImage_t* pDstImage,
00440                                          const HxRectangle_t* pSrcRect,
00441                                          const HxRectangle_t* pDstRect,
00442                                          HxBlitFlags_t flags);

00614  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.  Returns
00615  *                              HX_INVALID_ARG if pImage was not
00616  *                              properly initilialize by HxImageNew.
00617  *
00618  **/
00619 HxResult HxImageGetProperties(HxImage_t* pImage,
00620                               int32_t* pWidth, int32_t* pHeight,

00623 /**
00624  * @brief               Lock the display, and get a pointer to its data
00625  *
00626  * HxImageLockSurface is the accessor to the data pointer for the pixel
00627  * buffer associated with an offscreen canvas.
00628  *
00629  * In order to get the pointer to the pixel buffer, the pixel buffer must be
00630  * locked down.  This prevents other threads from trying to draw to the pixel
00631  * buffer at the same time.  While holding this lock, no other drawing can
00632  * occur.  Any attempt to draw will not cause an error, but the new data will
00633  * be ignored and not transferred to the canvas, even when the surface is
00634  * later unlocked.
00635  *
00636  * Consequently, the application must be very careful when using this API.
00637  * Every call to HxImageLockSurface must have a matching call to
00638  * HxImageUnlockSurface.  And care must be taken during the locked phase: the
00639  * application should not allow the event loop to run, which could cause a
00640  * screen update to get lost.
00641  *
00642  * @param pWindow       IN:     Pointer to an offscreen canvas
00643  * @param hDstBuf       OUT:    Handle to the canvas's pixel buffer
00644  *
00645  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.  Returns
00646  *                              HX_INVALID_ARG if pImage was not
00647  *                              properly initilialize by HxImageNew.
00648  *
00649  **/
00650 HxResult HxImageLockSurface(HxImage_t* pImage, void** hDstBuf);
00651 
00652 
00653 /**
00654  * @brief               Unlock the display
00655  *
00656  * HxImageUnlockSurface unlocks a surface that was locked due to a prior
00657  * call to HxImageLockSurface.
00658  *
00659  * @param pWindow       IN:     Pointer to an offscreen canvas
00660  *
00661  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK on success.
00662  *
00663  **/
00664 HxResult HxImageUnlockSurface(HxImage_t* pImage);
